checklist_items.1.1: The create dialog shows one field and none is hidden. Name is a required textbox, its value is empty, it has no unit and no control range. Reading the field sends no key write. The submit sends POST /api/v1/apikeys with only name. The 201 response carries that name. After reload the row shows the name and the prefix. The independent GET item keeps name, prefix and created_at

partial.12.7: The confirmation carries the name and the consequence and both are asserted: the product's own string with {{name}} replaced must be visible inside the viewport, and it reads 'Revoke <name>? Programs using it lose access at once; its past usage stays in Usage analytics. If no active tokens remain, the gateway allows anonymous access (development mode).' Cancelling it is required to send no mutation and to leave the token still authenticating /v1/models. What keeps this binding below the strongest form is a contract difference rather than an absent assertion: this resource is revoked, not deleted. DELETE /api/v1/apikeys/{prefix} answers {'status': 'revoked'} and the row stays listed carrying revoked_at, which the product's own test pins down as TestAPIKeyRevokeKeepsTheKeyListed (internal/server/api/apikey_validation_test.go:85), including a second revoke answering 200 with revoked_at unmoved at :121-125 - a delete is not idempotent that way. The case asserts the same shape from the outside: the active set is filtered by revoked_at, the revoked token appears in revoked rather than active, and it stops authenticating. So the name/impact and the failed-path halves of a delete confirmation have no object here: there is no destructive removal of the record, no in-use reference that could block a revoke, and therefore no half-applied-change half to prove. Recorded as the resource's own contract rather than as untested ground.

checklist_items.1.15: covered: Tab from the field stays inside the dialog across eight presses, Shift+Tab returns to the field, and the focus ring inherits theme.primary. At the recorded 1440x900 viewport the dialog and its submit button are each measured in a single frame after the open animation settles and must both sit inside the viewport with the button's rectangle wholly inside the dialog's, so neither the field nor the footer action can be clipped or overlapped.
checklist_items.7.1: The create dialog carries exactly one field and it is not a credential, so the masked and reveal halves of 7.1 have nothing to act on here - the key is generated by the server and shown once after creation, which is 7.3. Everything the single field does have is asserted. The field is inventoried before anything is typed: one textbox, the name label, empty, the declared placeholder, aria-required, no maxlength, no unit, no number input, and no radio, combobox or switch anywhere in the dialog, with exactly one form item and none hidden. Reading it is asserted to send no key write. Then the empty string and a whitespace-only value are each submitted and required to show the product's nameRequired message on the dialog, to mark the field aria-invalid, and to leave the mutation record empty. Proven by mutation: dropping whitespace:true from the name rule in APIKeysPage makes the case fail on the aria-invalid attribute for the whitespace value.
checklist_items.7.2: N/A: this component has no edit operation. The management API exposes only GET, POST and DELETE for these credentials, and the card offers create and revoke only, so there is no edit form whose blank field could mean either keep or clear. Replacing a credential means creating a new one and revoking the old, which is what the case already does.
checklist_items.7.5: The three credential planes are kept apart by shape and by what each one authorises, and both halves are asserted. The inference key is required to be a 51-character value starting with gw-, so it cannot be mistaken for a platform token, and the platform token is separately required to start with gwp_. The behaviour split is asserted with real requests rather than by reading a field: the inference key is accepted as a Bearer credential on /v1/models and refused with 401 once a character is appended, while the same key against the management route /api/v1/nodes is refused with 401 and AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED - so an inference key never stands in for a management session. The expiry side is not invented: inference keys expose no expiry control at all, which the field inventory asserts, and the platform token's own lifetime is asserted by its own case, so no expiry widget is claimed where the product has none.
checklist_items.7.6: No credential value the component holds is exposed by a read, an error or an artifact. The independent GET is required to return an exact field set - name, prefix and created_at - with the prefix being the first twelve characters, so the stored form is a hash and a prefix and the full secret is never recoverable from it. The DOM is asserted to contain no occurrence of the secret and so is the whole persisted collection, and the row is required to show only the prefix. The error plane is asserted too: a tampered secret sharing a valid prefix is refused with 401 and the product's fixed invalid-key body, which is a constant message rather than an echo of anything sent. The server log is written out through the artifact redactor and the artifacts are scanned, with a scan failure failing the run, so a secret reaching a log or a download rejects the artifacts rather than shipping them. Proven by mutation: storing the full token as the prefix in CreatePlatformToken makes the case fail on the token prefix.
